findings.reason: the §7 claim that "every existing caller is unchanged" is only true for the MAST row; the plan must name all four resolver consumers or fold them behind one machine-taking entry so a new machine cannot be half-wired.
findings.text: the plan keys the geometry registry by machine but names only `identity_for_shot` as the site that receives the declared machine, while four public resolvers default to `default_registry()` — `identity_for_representation` (line 187), `identity_for_shot` (216), `identity_for_table` (241) and `same_machine` (259) — so a JT-60SA caller of any of the other three still resolves MAST's packaged registry, and if the key becomes required all four call sites must be re-threaded rather than one named

findings.reason: one machine-configuration record keyed by machine, owning the pin, the frozen shot set and the registry key together, would make "add a machine" one edit and remove the coordination the plan currently relies on a reader to perform.
findings.text: machine-keyed configuration is split into three parallel tables in three modules with no single owner: the pin table here (`PINNED_SEMANTIC_IDENTITY`/`PINNED_PHYSICAL_DIGEST`/`PINNED_REGISTRY_DIGEST` becoming a machine-keyed table), the frozen shot-set table in imas_ambix/spine_bench/shots.py:19/42 (`SHOTSET_VERSION`/`FROZEN_SHOTSET` becoming machine-keyed) and the registry key in imas_ambix/gs/machine_identity.py:145 (`default_registry` becoming machine-keyed), each of which a new machine must be added to by hand and which the plan itself relies on staying consistent (the `SetupSignature.key` collision it guards against arises when one is missed)

findings.reason: a single `resolve_machine(machine)` returning the pin, the frozen set, the registry and the reader would hide the coordination behind one interface instead of exposing four keyed lookups to the caller.
findings.text: §7 threads the declared machine as a bare string through four shallow sites (the pin table lookup, the shot-set lookup, `default_registry(machine)` and the newly-required `MachineArtifactGeometryReader.machine` at imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py:758) rather than behind one deep resolver, so the route's machine-awareness is the sum of four independently-edited pass-throughs and a missed one fails only at the point it is exercised

findings.reason: the counts for this week are all zero and the section does name its one public addition and its three retirements; this is a completeness note on the same defect already reported under duplicate_owner, not an independent interface-budget gap.
findings.text: the pin-table change is stated to "declare all four files as its scope" and the required-argument change to retire "one default", but the section does not name the four resolvers of `default_registry` as consumers of the key it introduces, so the added machine key is accounted against the surface it retires only partially.

response_events.reason: The three machine-keyed tables stay separate owners because they own different things: the pin table is a frozen expectation recorded at stamping that must not be derived from the registry it guards, and the frozen shot set is the benchmark's declaration in spine_bench, which gs does not and must not import. The half-wiring risk is closed instead by ArtifactMachineSelector being the one machine-taking entry, refusing by name at construction a machine absent from the pin table or the registry (plan s7, commit 53d71d81).

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §7 makes the machine-aware route a hand-threaded machine key through three separate tables and a newly-required constructor argument, with no single module that owns "the machines ambix knows and their per-machine configuration", so a JT-60SA run is machine-aware only where each site was individually edited.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-homes machine identity in three modules at once (a pin table in `gs/artifact_resolution.py`, a frozen-shot-set table in `spine_bench/shots.py`, and a machine key on `gs/machine_identity.default_registry`) and names only one of the four resolvers that consume the default registry, so the machine is a second owner copied across modules rather than one owner extended.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; each section that adds surface names in its own text what it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be (§2: seven exporter names, "none of the seven retires anything"; §6: three EQDB types and two `BatchResult` fields, "they retire nothing, because no equilibrium-database request type exists"; §7: the pin table adds one and retires three exported pins and their re-export, and the required `machine` argument retires one default).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched both named repositories and cites the owner of each mechanism it extends or reuses (§2 collapses scale through the engine's `transform_engine.py` and flags the exporter's duplicate resolver; §6 reuses `cocos_convention.score_convention`, `challenge/convention._integrated_current`, `description_reader.read_geometry_table` and `VirtualZarrView.raw_series`; §7 reuses `eval/efit_referee.judge_geometry`, `worldmodel/equilibrium_labels.build_geometry_from_arrays` and `MachineArtifactGeometrySource`), so no proposed mechanism rebuilds an existing one.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every added layer carries an explicit why-not-extend justification in its own text (§2 keeps the exporter out of the loaders because they must not learn tokamap's format; §6 adds EQDB request/record/refusal types rather than widening the channel-shaped ones, because `ChannelRequest` is keyed `(shot, category, dname)` and an EQDB record is psi on a 2-D grid; §7 refuses a JT-60SA key in `transform_geometry_source.resolve_geometry_source` because it would give the stamp a different reader from the spine).
